dedupe_keys.name: usgs brit bridge risk interactive tool site specific highway bridge seismic risk under hazard model epistemic uncertainty

description: brit is a USGS Python package and Jupyter dashboard (Kwong and Jaiswal 2022, DOI 10.5066/P9N5QTIN) published on code.usgs.gov. Contents: the notebook launches an interactive dashboard showing a site-specific seismic risk assessment of a highway bridge from an input hazard curve for 1-second spectral acceleration; users switch Hazus highway bridge class, damage state, fractile hazard curves and fragility dispersion in a sidebar and the plots and risk estimates update. Default fragility curves come from Table 7-6 of the Hazus earthquake technical manual, and hazard curves can come from different USGS National Seismic Hazard Model versions, VS30 estimates or logic-tree branches. Producer: USGS (N.S. Kwong and K.S. Jaiswal). Coverage: any site with a hazard curve, framed around the US hazard models. Format and access: open source Python (numpy, pandas, scipy, panel, holoviews) with unit tests reported at 99% coverage. Licence: CC0 1.0 (repository licence). Caveats: the dashboard supports only 1-second spectral acceleration although the package handles 0.2-second too; the accompanying journal paper was in review when the README was written; the last repository activity was January 2023. Simulation uses: bridge fragility and risk inputs for road network resilience studies, and sensitivity of bridge loss estimates to hazard uncertainty. Related records: data-usgs-national-seismic-hazard-model, data-fhwa-national-bridge-inventory and platform-hazus.
